ruleName: Moving Loose Impediments and Movable Obstructions
title: Can You Move a Worm Before Playing?
question: Your ball comes to rest in the rough. A large worm is lying directly behind your ball and is likely to interfere with your next shot. Can you move the worm before playing?

choices.text: No. Animals on the course must never be moved.
Yes. A live worm is an animal and may be moved without penalty.
Yes, but only if your ball is on the putting green.
No. You must either play the ball as it lies or take an unplayable ball.

explanation: A live worm is an animal and may be moved without penalty, regardless of where the ball lies. However, if moving the worm causes your ball at rest to move, you must replace the ball and may incur a penalty unless an exception applies. This is detailed in the Definition of Animal, and Rules 9 and 8.1a of the Rules of Golf.
